chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
That the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) provided the grandmother with one-sixth, and did not legislate anything specific for her.

key_terms.أَطْعَمَ: Provided with food/share (metaphor for giving inheritance)

ai.seo_question: What is the share of the grandmother in Islamic inheritance according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the grandmother's share as one-sixth (suds) based on the Prophet’s practice, a ruling central to Shia jurisprudence for determining inheritance when parents are absent. The phrase 'did not legislate anything' is interpreted by scholars to mean that while the one-sixth is fixed, no additional specific share was assigned beyond this, distinguishing it from the mother's or father's portions. This narration serves as a primary textual basis for the calculation of fractional shares in the absence of direct ascendants.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>
that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> provided the grandmother with the one-sixth, and did not Obligate (legislate) anything for her’.
en.sarwar: 13. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, provided for the grandmother one-sixth but did not sanction anything for her.’”
